newsitem.title: USA: UCAR sees Q4 EPS between $0.68 to $0.78.
newsitem.headline: UCAR sees Q4 EPS between $0.68 to $0.78.

text.p: UCAR International said on Wednesday it expected fourth quarter earnings between $0.68 and $0.78 per share, compared to $0.65 per share in the same quarter last year, due to a shortfall in graphic electrode shipments to customers in Europe and the Middle East.
The company said this was below analysts' expectations. The First Call mean earnings estimate was $0.81 per share for the quarter.
UCAR said it expected fiscal 1996 earnings to be between $2.90 and $3.00 per share compared to proforma earnings of $1.87 per share last year.
The 1996 earnings projections excluded a gain of $0.15 per share for the cumulative effect on prior years of a change in accounting for inventories.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for fiscal 1996 was $3.04 per share.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Robert Krass said despite the shortfall in graphic electrodes volumes, the long term outlook for growth in electric steel remained promising.
The company said excluding the impact of intended acquisitions, it expected its 1997 earnings to be at least 15 percent above 1996 earnings.
Demand for electrodes, which are consumed in the electric steel making process, was expected to grow at a long-term rate of one to two percent per year, Krass said.

"We have not experienced and do not expect any material change in our global market share for graphic electrodes," Krass said, adding that the pricing environment remained favorable. He said the company had already implemented price increases for 1997.
